title: Uniform equivariant comparison with the ordered join of cosets
statement:
Let $G$ be a group, $H\subseteq G$ a subgroup, $n\geq1$ and $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in G$. For a set $Y$, let $B_q(Y)$, $q\geq0$, be the free abelian group with specified basis the ordered $(q+1)$-tuples $[y_0,\ldots,y_q]$, with repeated entries allowed [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Put $B_{-1}(Y)=\mathbf Z$ on the empty tuple and $B_q(Y)=0$ for $q<-1$. The boundary $d$ is alternating deletion, with $d[y]=1$ and $d(1)=0$ in degree $-1$. On $B_q(H)$ and $B_q(G)$ the action of $H$ is diagonal left translation, trivial in degree $-1$.
Let $X_i=Ha_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, as separately labeled sets, and let $J_q$ be the ordered-join groups with basis $[(i_0,x_0),\ldots,(i_q,x_q)]$, $i_0<\cdots<i_q$, $x_j\in Ha_{i_j}$, augmentation $J_{-1}=\mathbf Z$ and alternating deletion boundary, as in [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] for $r=n+1$. Let $H$ act on $J_q$ by left translation of every vertex, $g[(i_0,x_0),\ldots,(i_q,x_q)]=[(i_0,gx_0),\ldots,(i_q,gx_q)]$ for $g\in H$ (each $Ha_i$ is stable under left translation by $H$), and trivially on $J_{-1}$. For $h\in H$, let $S^h$ be the explicit operator $S$ defined in that node with chosen vertices $v_i(h)=ha_i$. Define $P_q:B_q(H)\to J_q$ on basis symbols, extended additively, by
$$P_{-1}=1,\qquad P_0[h_0]=[(0,h_0a_0)],\qquad P_q[h_0,\ldots,h_q]=S^{h_0}_{q-1}\bigl(P_{q-1}(d[h_0,\ldots,h_q])\bigr)\quad(1\leq q\leq n).$$
Then $dP_q=P_{q-1}d$ for $0\leq q\leq n$, and $P_q(gz)=gP_q(z)$ for $g\in H$ in all degrees $-1\leq q\leq n$.
For each $0\leq q\leq n$ there is a fixed finite list of integers $c_\lambda$, strictly increasing color lists $i_{\lambda,0}<\cdots<i_{\lambda,q}$ in $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and indices $j_{\lambda,k}\in\{0,\ldots,q\}$ such that, for all $h_0,\ldots,h_q\in H$,
$$P_q[h_0,\ldots,h_q]=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda[(i_{\lambda,0},h_{j_{\lambda,0}}a_{i_{\lambda,0}}),\ldots,(i_{\lambda,q},h_{j_{\lambda,q}}a_{i_{\lambda,q}})].$$
The entire list is independent of the values of the $h_j$; repeated formal terms may be retained, so no equality test on vertices is required.
Erasing color labels defines homomorphisms $e_q:J_q\to B_q(G)$, with $e_{-1}=1$. They commute with $d$ and with $H$-translation. Consequently $A_q=e_qP_q$ is an $H$-equivariant augmented chain map through degree $n$, with $A_{-1}=1$. In degree $n$, its image is contained in the integer span of tuples $[h_0a_0,\ldots,h_na_n]$ with $h_i\in H$.

proof.text: Apply the recursive comparison lemma for the chain-map and input-independent finite-formula clauses. Its proof uses the original contraction induction and color-only expansion. Equivariance is proved separately by induction on arity: tuple maps commute with deletion, the chosen vertices for h translate to those for gh, and naturality of the contraction gives the induction step. The arity-zero and arity-one cases are evaluated directly on basis vectors.

Apply erasure-boundary compatibility for every integer degree. Check erasure equivariance on Finsupp basis vectors: mapping the vertex list by left multiplication is the same as translating each colored vertex before taking the list. The tuple-map evaluation on tupleTerm follows directly from its linearCombination definition and preservation of length.

The arity-zero comparison has a constant basis value, so linearCombination is total coefficient sum times the empty face. A degree-minus-one colored symbol has cardinality zero and hence no colors; its erased list is empty. This proves both augmentation formulas, and erasure sends the empty face to the empty tuple.

Compose the comparison and erasure identities by associativity of linear maps to obtain chain-map and equivariance identities for A=eP. Handle the equality arityDegree(q)=q-1 separately in the zero and successor cases to avoid dependent index transports. Apply the proved comparison augmentation and linearity of erasure to obtain A_{-1}=1.

In fact erasure of every degree-n join chain lies in the desired span, independently of P. A degree-n symbol has n+1 colors, so its color set equals all of Fin(n+1). Each vertex therefore supplies a witness h_i∈H for x_i=h_i a_i. Its erased list is ofFn(i↦h_i a_i), a generator of the stated span. Extend by finite sums and scalar multiplication, then apply this to P of the input chain.

lean.statement: theorem orderedJoinCosetComparison (H : Subgroup G) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (a : Fin (n + 1) → G) : (∀ q : ℕ, q ≤ n → (boundary (Coset H a) (q : ℤ) (arityDegree q)).comp (comparison H a (q + 1)) = (comparison H a q).comp (tupleBoundary H (q : ℤ) (arityDegree q))) ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ n + 1 → ∀ g : H, (comparison H a k).comp (tupleMap (fun h : H ↦ g * h) (arityDegree k)) = (chainMap (translateVertex H a g) (arityDegree k)).comp (comparison H a k)) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, q ≤ n → ∃ L : List (ℤ × Symbol (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) ↦ Fin (q + 1)) (q : ℤ)), ∀ h : Fin (q + 1) → H, comparison H a (q + 1) (tupleTerm (q : ℤ) (List.ofFn h)) = (L.map (fun t ↦ t.1 • chainMap (fun i j ↦ vertex H a (h j) i) (q : ℤ) (Finsupp.single t.2 1))).sum) ∧ (∀ q : ℤ, (tupleBoundary G q (q - 1)).comp (erasure H a q) = (erasure H a (q - 1)).comp (boundary (Coset H a) q (q - 1))) ∧ (∀ (q : ℤ) (g : H), (erasure H a q).comp (chainMap (translateVertex H a g) q) = (tupleMap (fun x : G ↦ (g : G) * x) q).comp (erasure H a q)) ∧ (∀ z : TupleChain H (-1), comparison H a 0 z = (z.sum (fun _ m ↦ m)) • symbolTerm (Coset H a) (-1) ⟨∅, fun i hi ↦ False.elim (Finset.notMem_empty i hi)⟩) ∧ (∀ z : Chain (Coset H a) (-1), erasure H a (-1) z = (z.sum (fun _ m ↦ m)) • tupleTerm (-1) ([] : List G)) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, q ≤ n → (tupleBoundary G (q : ℤ) (arityDegree q)).comp (erasedComparison H a (q + 1)) = (erasedComparison H a q).comp (tupleBoundary H (q : ℤ) (arityDegree q))) ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ), k ≤ n + 1 → ∀ g : H, (erasedComparison H a k).comp (tupleMap (fun h : H ↦ g * h) (arityDegree k)) = (tupleMap (fun x : G ↦ (g : G) * x) (arityDegree k)).comp (erasedComparison H a k)) ∧ (∀ z : TupleChain H (-1), erasedComparison H a 0 z = (z.sum (fun _ m ↦ m)) • tupleTerm (-1) ([] : List G)) ∧ LinearMap.range (erasedComparison H a (n + 1)) ≤ Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range (fun h : Fin (n + 1) → H ↦ tupleTerm (n : ℤ) (List.ofFn (fun i ↦ (h i : G) * a i))))
